items.title: Planktonic hyperiidean amphipod confirmed in the Aegean Sea, and a new study shows how to identify subadult males
items.summary: Amphipods change in size and shape each time they molt. When a species is told apart from its relatives by small anatomical details, this creates a practical problem: a trait that identifies an adult may be absent or different in the younger animal. A recently published study in Biodiversity Data Journal tests this problem on Phronima atlantica, a planktonic amphipod of the open ocean, and identifies which of its features stay reliable in males from the subadult to the adult stage.
